round1.cite: the in-flight command refuses a seat start on a stale probe
round1.reply:
Support-it
The design is minimal and enforceable: it turns a documented drift into a hard gate at seat launch, matching the 50-minute rule and preserving the override only for a no-driver read-only case. It does not change the underlying probe cadence, freshness threshold, or command-probe behavior; it only blocks stale evidence before writing anything. The evidence in card 297 shows actual stale probes caused user-visible risk, while the override is narrow, logged, and limited to real exceptions. This is low false-positive risk and easy to reverse.
CITE: the in-flight command refuses a seat start on a stale probe

round1.cite: inflight.sh) exits with an error and writes no in-flight line when
round1.reply:
Yes

The rule is testable red first. A fixture probe file aged 51 minutes must give exit 1, the message text, and a clean git state with nothing written, committed or pushed. A 49-minute probe must pass. Because the refusal comes before any write, a bad line can't get through the check.

Two cases the red tests should cover: a missing or empty probes directory, and a probe timestamp in the future. Both must refuse and not pass. The override should also be tested: the reason text must be present in the line, and an empty `INFLIGHT_STALE_OK` must not count as set.

The metric, 8 of 14, can be counted from existing lines.

CITE: inflight.sh) exits with an error and writes no in-flight line when

round1.cite: No seat starts without an in-flight line
round1.reply:
Support-it

The refusal is workable and fair: it centralizes F-085 enforcement before any backend seat starts, adds no seat ceremony when the probe is fresh, and preserves a narrow, counted escape hatch for genuinely driverless work. The three-card trial, latency counter-metric, and override count expose gaming. C2 should specify how the mandatory override reason is supplied; the variable shown carries only authorization, not the reason required in the line. That ambiguity is small enough to resolve during implementation.

CITE: No seat starts without an in-flight line

round1.cite: exits with an error and writes no in-flight line when the newest probe
round1.reply:
Support-it

The metric can be checked from git alone. The committed in-flight lines record last-probe age, and card 297's 8 of 14 is a count you can re-derive. The refusal also moves the rule into the tool.

Two loopholes remain. The first is a seat started with no in-flight line, so the line never exists. Then it can't count as stale, and the metric reads 0. Add a check that seat-start commits match in-flight lines one to one. The second is INFLIGHT_STALE_OK=1, whose reason is free text. Count overrides with a grep on "stale probe override", and make them fail review if the seat did use a driver.

CITE: exits with an error and writes no in-flight line when the newest probe

round1.cite: No seat starts without an in-flight line
round1.reply:
Support-it

The baseline is concrete and auditable: 8 of 14 starts exceeded F-085, with recorded ages and repeated reminder failures. The three-card trial, counter-metrics, override count, and reversible enforcement support an evidence-based keep/revise/drop decision. All seven required perspectives contributed, and independent sign-off remains intact. At review, distinguish refused attempts, compliant starts, and overrides; otherwise “zero stale starts” is partly guaranteed by construction. C2 should also require a nonempty reason through a defined input, so overrides remain measurable rather than becoming an undocumented escape hatch.

CITE: No seat starts without an in-flight line
